structure.note: One class of common stock; 574,121,620 shares were outstanding on the April 14, 2025 record date. Nasdaq's charter generally bars any shareholder from voting more than 5% of total voting power, and an agreement limits Borse Dubai's voting power to 4.35%. Holders above 5%: Borse Dubai 10.2%, Investor AB 10.1%, Vanguard 9.1%, Thoma Bravo 7.5%, Wellington 6.8% and BlackRock 5.3%.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (matches data.js fy 'Dec 2024'). Filings: FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0001120193-25-000008) and 2025 proxy statement (accession 0001193125-25-100786), both read on www.sec.gov. ADENA FRIEDMAN: 2,752,108 shares, including 806,451 vested options and 147,000 shares in family trusts; less than 1% (marked * in the proxy), so pctEconomic is null. HOLDERS: the three largest are kept. Thoma Bravo (7.5%, via Argus Seller, LP), Wellington (6.8%) and BlackRock (5.3%) are left out by the three-holder limit and named in the structure note. The proxy reports each 'as of the record date' (April 14, 2025) but bases each on a 13D/13G filed on an earlier date (Borse Dubai Mar 22, 2024; Investor AB Nov 6, 2023; Vanguard Nov 12, 2024), so asOf is null. Investor AB's percentage is printed '10.1.%' in the proxy. Borse Dubai is typed 'company': the proxy describes it only as a wholly owned subsidiary of Investment Corporation of Dubai and does not state government ownership. In 2024 Borse Dubai sold 31.0 million shares and Thoma Bravo 42.8 million in secondary offerings. BUYBACKS exclude $60 million of 'Payments related to employee shares withheld for taxes'. ROUNDING: buybacks of $145 million are rounded half-up to 0.15. GEOGRAPHY: total revenues of $7,400 million are gross, before transaction-based expenses (the 10-K's 'revenues less transaction-based expenses' were $4,649 million).
